thread:
maya: heads-up — noticed a sharp p99 API latency bump correlated with trace pipeline CPU on the otel-collector pods.
maya: Around 11:04 UTC we started seeing p99 jump from ~180ms -> ~420ms, coincident with trace_exporter_cpu_percent on infra nodes hitting 70%.
sam: ugh, did we change sampling or are spans exploding from a rollout?
sam: any recent client changes that add lots of attributes / events per span?
lucy: no deploys touching tracing yesterday. alerted by SLOs. I pulled the otel metrics: receiver_spans_total rose from 3k/s -> ~12k/s around 11:02.
andrew: that's a lot. what exporter are we using? otlp/http or grpc?
maya: grpc to our internal collector -> jaeger backend. collector shows exporter queue growing and frequent flushes.
infra-bot: [alert] otel-collector-pool-3 cpu 72% | exporter_queue_length 12400 | flush_duration_p99 1.2s
lucy: can we try increasing batch size & timeout to reduce exporter overhead? also enable compress/gzip on otlp exporter.
sam: agree. try batch_size 512, send_timeout 300ms as an experiment. also limit max_concurrency of exporter to avoid overwhelming CPU.
andrew: note: batch tuning trades latency for CPU — but should cut per-span overhead. let's also test switching OTLP to grpc_keepalive disabled? and gzip compression.
maya: I'll spin a canary config on one collector replica. patch I plan to apply (kubectl edit configmap otel-collector-config):

```
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "collector-internal:4317"
    compression: gzip
    timeout: 5s

processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 512
    send_batch_timeout: 300ms
    timeout: 10s
    # cap concurrency to avoid single-thread spike
    # (collector-specific processor settings)

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```

maya: applying to collector-canary-1 now.
sam: also add a quick metric on span_size_bytes distribution — if spans got huge we need to consider attribute trimming.
lucy: good call. I deployed a patch to strip trace.attributes['raw_payload'] for a week — that attribute was ~5-10KB often.
andrew: once canary is up, watch these metrics: collector_cpu, exporter_queue_length, batch_flush_duration_p50/p99, and api_p99.
infra-bot: [deploy] configmap/otel-collector-config updated on collector-canary-1 at 1768124952
maya: canary shows cpu down from 72% -> 38% on that pod within 90s, exporter_queue_length dropped from 8k -> 200, api_p99 decreased ~15% after backend ingestion got smoother.
sam: nice. what about end-to-end tracing fidelity? any lost spans?
lucy: no loss observed. batching increased per-span latency by ~3ms but overall tail improved. sampling stayed same.
andrew: next steps: roll to majority of collectors, add gzip for all exporters, and add automated alert for receiver_spans_total > 6k/s to trigger batching escalation.
maya: opened a short RFC in #eng-platform with rollback plan and metrics to keep an eye on. I'll schedule a post-rollout check in 1 hour.
sam: also let's add a cheap tail-based sampler prototype for noisy services; can reduce total spans without losing critical traces.
lucy: noted. will follow up with a small PR to strip a few heavy attributes at agent-level as a safety belt.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
